description: The planned experiments (EXPERIMENTS.md). Each step changes one group of settings, scored on one frozen case set. A side either runs (profile + modes) or reuses another step's saved run at no cost.

steps.title: Council versus single agent
steps.question: Does a council beat one agent?
steps.changes: The reviewer: one agent, then the Analyst / Skeptic / Chair council. The evidence and settings stay at the base profile.
steps.repeat_note: The council is run twice with identical settings; the difference between the two runs is the noise between identical runs.

steps.title: Council versus single agent, with more code
steps.question: Does the council beat one agent once the AI sees more of the code?
steps.changes: The reviewer, as in step 1, but at the evidence profile (60 lines either side plus related source). Step 1 compared them at the base profile; this tests whether the council's value depends on the evidence it gets.

steps.title: Council versus single agent, with more code and the worksheet
steps.question: Does the council beat one agent once the AI also fills in the reasoning worksheet?
steps.changes: The reviewer, as in step 1, but at the worksheet profile (more code plus the reasoning worksheet and consistency repair).

steps.title: More of the code
steps.question: Does showing the AI more of the code help?
steps.changes: The evidence: source window 25 to 60 lines either side, and related source (called methods, other files, referenced scripts) switched on.

steps.title: Reasoning worksheet
steps.question: Does a reasoning worksheet with a consistency check help?
steps.changes: The output: a structured analysis (source, sink, reaches the sink, protection, protection effective) is required, and a verdict that contradicts it gets one repair call.

steps.title: Semantic retrieval
steps.question: Does semantic retrieval hold up?
steps.changes: The guidance source: the hand-made CWE table is replaced by semantic search over the OWASP cheat sheets, anchored on the alert's MITRE CWE record, with the set-up rules R1-R5 fixed before measuring (design decision 28). Built on step 2 (evidence profile, council); the worksheet from step 3 showed no benefit and is not carried forward.
steps.rule: Agreed in advance: if semantic retrieval holds or improves accuracy on the comparison set, it is reported as an improvement. If not, it stays the design choice, argued on scalability and maintainability, and the accuracy difference is stated plainly. Any tuning happens on exploration cases only, followed by one measurement on the comparison set.

steps.title: Mutation test
steps.question: Does the verdict follow the code?
steps.changes: The code: in each case one constant condition is flipped ('num > 200' to 'num < 200', the same length, so no line moves), which flips which branch runs and so the right verdict. Before: the originals; after: their mutants, each read from its own overlay root (the Benchmark source with only the mutated file replaced), so both are judged on the same evidence except that line. Both sides run the final version (the semantic profile), single agent and council, on one commit.
steps.cost_note: From the recorded per-case costs on the comparison set (as step 6): council US$1.3955 / 96 cases in 4-after (semantic profile); single agent US$0.4146 / 96 in 1b-before (the same evidence; step 4 ran the council only). 22 pairs, both sides, both modes: 4 runs of 22 cases, 176 calls, about US$0.83.
steps.rule: A pair counts only if the reviewer got the original right. Killed: the mutant's verdict is the flipped right answer. Survived: the verdict is unchanged. Escalated: the mutant was sent to a human; reported separately, not a kill. Mutation score = killed / pairs that meet the precondition, per configuration and per direction. `experiment run 5` refuses uncommitted changes to tracked files and a commit other than the one a saved run of step 5 recorded.

steps.title: Headline result
steps.question: How well does the final system do on cases it has never seen?
steps.changes: Nothing is changed: the final version (the semantic profile, design decision 29), single agent and council, run once on the unseen final test after the code freeze.
steps.cost_note: From the recorded per-case costs on the comparison set: council US$1.3955 / 96 cases in 4-after (semantic profile); single agent US$0.4146 / 96 in 1b-before (the evidence profile, the same evidence; step 4 ran the council only). For 120 cases: about US$0.52 single + US$1.75 council.
steps.rule: The final test is run once. `experiment run 6` refuses a working tree with uncommitted changes to tracked files (the run records the commit it ran on) and refuses a fresh run once a run has results; an interrupted run resumes. Starting over needs --i-know-this-reruns-the-final-test.
